title: Lansing Mayor Andy Schor delivers 2026 State of the City - NewsBreak
text:
By Shajaka Shelton Zack Priehs ,
7 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — Lansing Mayor Andy Schor delivered the annual State of the City” address. He says Lansing is in a very good place moving into the heart of 2026, largely due to billions of dollars’ worth of new investments.
Schor spoke about everything from Lansing’s job market to the upcoming Lugnuts season, but one recent development stands out — the recent agreement by Tesla to purchase car batteries from a plant in Lansing. The deal is worth $4 billion and Schor says it will produce 1,700 jobs when all said and done.
Mayor Schor says the new deal puts Lansing in a great spot moving forward.
“Large, that’s not even including the $2.3 billion that was spent in building it and building out the assembly lines,” said Schor. “And that was a great impact to our trades workers who are basically now at full employment, and now these great paying 1,700 jobs, it’s an immense impact in our city.”
Schor also celebrated the Lansing Police Department, touting less homicides than the year before, as well as a decrease in all shootings.
Andy Schor. (WLNS) The mayor also praised the Human Resources and Community Services Department (HRCS), who says they are hard at work with safety net programs like mod-pods and coat drives.
“Last year, HRCS led the 7th annual coat drive, the Lets Share the Warmth Coat Drive, which led to the collection of over 900 coats. In addition to the coats, we collected a substantial amount of gloves, earmuffs and scarves for those in need, said Delvata Moses, the programs interim Director.
Finally, the mayor discussed the roads.
He says Lansing has recently increased its funding going to road construction … and encouraged the public to call the 3-1-1 helpline to report potholes.
Andy Kilpatrick, the city’s public service director, says this year, there will be a special focus on fixing neighborhood roads.
“We figured maybe we’d get another 9-ish miles of roads that we would not have done other than this funding,” said Kilpatrick. “A lot of the need has been in neighborhoods, so you’ll see a lot going on in neighborhoods over the next several years.”
Another big project looming in Lansing is the potential Deep Green Data Center.
6 News spoke to multiple Lansing city councilmen Wednesday and all of them said they still have yet to make their final decision on whether they’ll vote “yes” or “no.” on the data center.
